solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, directions as headed, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A service provided by aging poet

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services
aging means old

explanation.surface: Someone getting on in years is being looked after by some kind of service.
explanation.walkthrough: Matthew Arnold was a Victorian poet, best known for 'Dover Beach'.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew Arnold was a celebrated nineteenth-century English poet and critic.

clue.text: Attraction to see when rounding up King of England

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole build is read from the bottom upwards
rounding means the word for see goes around the word for attraction

parts.note: vide is Latin for 'see', used in references
a draw is something that attracts crowds

explanation.surface: Something attractive is worth a look when collecting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounding' and 'up' work together: in a down clue 'up' turns the whole container round, giving VIDRAWDE read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward the Fourth was a Yorkist monarch who reigned over England in the fifteenth century.

clue.text: 'Fly Emirates' pilots at terminal missing revised map of descent

indicators.note: revised means the remaining letters are reworked into a new order
missing means that final letter is taken out of the airline slogan
at terminal points to the final letter of the word pilots

explanation.surface: An airline's pilots at the airport terminal lack an updated route map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops S (the last of 'pilots') from FLYEMIRATES; 'revised' rearranges FLYEMIRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A genealogical chart traces a family's line of ancestry, a map showing who descended from whom.

clue.text: Sweet jar bottomless, holding breadbasket on cycle in reserve

indicators.note: holding means the shortened jar wraps around the cycled stomach word
bottomless means the last letter, the bottom of a down entry, is removed

parts.note: taken as the word jar itself

indicators.note: on cycle means the first letter of the stomach word goes round to the end

parts.note: breadbasket is slang for the stomach or belly
by means aside, kept in reserve, as in 'put by'

explanation.surface: A sweet jar with no bottom, containing the cyclist's stomach, kept spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottomless' cuts JAR to JA; 'on cycle' turns BELLY into ELLYB, which JA holds, then BY is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Jelly babies are soft gummy confectionery shaped like infants, a classic British sweet.

clue.text: All right to dress her up?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
to dress here means to clothe, so the words all right cover the answer inside them

explanation.surface: Is it fine to get her dressed up?
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'All right' backwards and THGIRLLA shows the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl is a young female, referred to by the pronoun her.

clue.text: Resident of South Africa up for a brew?

parts.note: up for means keen on, in favour of: pro
a brew is a cup of tea

explanation.surface: Is this South African local keen on a cup of tea?
explanation.walkthrough: The king protea is South Africa's national flower, so it is fairly a resident there.
explanation.definitionFit: Proteas are flowering shrubs native to South Africa, where one species is the national flower.

clue.text: Historical debauchee and king, when introduced

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
as can mean when, as in 'as the sun rose'
put in means introduced or inserted

explanation.surface: A notorious libertine of history and a monarch were brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: Grigori Rasputin was the Russian mystic at the court of the last Tsar, notorious for drink and womanising.

clue.text: What distinguishes ginger nuts as hardier?

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of hardier go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Are ginger nut biscuits tougher than other kinds?
explanation.walkthrough: 'ginger nuts' looks like the biscuit; 'ginger' is a redhead and 'nuts' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A person nicknamed Ginger is so called for their flame-coloured locks.

clue.text: Border missing edge of iron band

indicators.note: missing means taking away; here the letters of the iron symbol, which sit at the edges, are removed

parts.note: a fringe is a border or edge
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A metal band lacks a border at its edge.
explanation.walkthrough: F and E, the symbol for iron, are the two ends of FRINGE, hence 'edge'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring is a circular band, such as one worn on a finger.

clue.text: Educated hairdresser about moving in near East African location

indicators.note: near means the east letter is placed beside the rest

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

indicators.note: moving in means the word for about goes inside the hairdresser's name

parts.note: Rita is the hairdresser in Willy Russell's play and film 'Educating Rita'
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A schooled hairdresser is relocating to somewhere close to East Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Educating Rita' is a 1983 British film about a hairdresser who takes an Open University course; 'moving in' signals the container and 'near' the placing beside.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a country in the Horn of Africa, on the Red Sea coast.

clue.text: Eggs smashed in a lot of big hands?

parts.note: ova are eggs, the plural of ovum

indicators.note: smashed means the letters of in a lot are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Many large hands smash some eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'big hand' is a round of applause, so 'of big hands' means relating to ovations.
explanation.definitionFit: A big hand is warm applause, and the adjective relates to standing ovations.

clue.text: Stopped Blue Peter broadcast short of brewing beer

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters of Blue Peter are rearranged
short of means without; brewing says the letters of beer are removed in any order

explanation.surface: A children's TV programme stopped airing because no beer was being made.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue Peter is a long-running BBC children's programme; take B, E, E, R out of its letters and rearrange LUPET.
explanation.definitionFit: To let up is to ease off or cease, so the past tense means paused or ceased.

clue.text: Top of the Pops?

parts.note: pops are fathers, and the top one among them is the biggest father of all; also a famous BBC chart show

explanation.surface: A reference to the BBC chart show 'Top of the Pops'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top of the Pops' was the BBC's weekly chart music programme; read 'pops' as fathers and 'top' as the chief one.
explanation.definitionFit: A father is affectionately called this, and 'the ___ of them all' means the biggest or best one.

clue.text: Rocky tables bearing fine port

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the rearranged tables hold the letter for fine
rocky means unsteady, so the letters of tables wobble into a new order

parts.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Wobbly tables carry a fine wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' rearranges TABLES to BELAST, and 'bearing' puts F inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Belfast is Northern Ireland's capital and a major harbour city, famous for shipbuilding.

clue.text: Raving lunatics stockpiling 24 oils?

indicators.note: stockpiling means holding in store, so the rearranged letters contain the piece from 24
raving means wild, so the letters of lunatics go mad into a new order

parts.note: the clue at 24 across begins 'Little brother', and the short form of brother is Br

explanation.surface: Mad people are hoarding a quantity of oils.
explanation.walkthrough: A clue number used as fodder can mean that clue's wordplay rather than its answer: here only 'Little brother' from 24 across is used, and 'stockpiling' puts it inside the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Oils are used as lubricants to reduce friction; the question mark flags that not every one is an oil.

clue.text: Anti-inflammatory in heart, with time, is working

indicators.note: in means the following pieces go inside the word for heart

parts.note: the core is the heart or centre of something
T is the physics abbreviation for time
on means working, as a machine that is switched on

explanation.surface: A drug that reduces swelling is acting on the heart, given time.
explanation.definitionFit: This steroid hormone is used medically to reduce swelling and inflammation.

clue.text: 'Biblical flowers' deciphered by brain of solver

indicators.note: deciphered means worked out, so the letters of by brain of solver are reordered

explanation.surface: A cryptic phrase about Bible flowers is decoded by the solver's brain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowers' wants to be blooms; here it means things that flow, the Tigris and Euphrates of Psalm 137.
explanation.definitionFit: Psalm 137 begins with the exiled Israelites weeping by the waters of that ancient Mesopotamian city.

clue.text: Means to secure enclosure in which you watch boxers escape

parts.words: enclosure in which you watch boxers
parts.note: boxing takes place in a ring
to bolt is to run off or escape

explanation.surface: A way to keep the boxers' arena locked so the dogs can't run off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxers' could be dogs, but here they are fighters in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringbolt is a bolt with a ring through its head, used for fastening ropes or securing things.

clue.text: I'm thinking I'd like to rent out Exeter or Ely, please

definitions.meaning: a phrase said while pausing to ponder

definitions.text: I'd like to rent out Exeter or Ely, please
definitions.meaning: a request to be leased a bishop's diocese; Exeter and Ely are cathedral cities, each a bishop's see

explanation.surface: Someone muses about asking to lease a cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is the diocese of a bishop, and Exeter and Ely are both English cathedral cities; 'let' means rent out.
explanation.definitionFit: Said while pondering, the phrase means 'give me a moment to consider'.

clue.text: A piece of cake to keep large women in trim?!

indicators.note: to keep means the word for trim holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: neat means trim or tidy
OS is the clothing size abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: Something easy to keep plus-size women in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer also suggests exercise without perspiring, which suits the slimming picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of cake is an easy task, and so is something requiring no effort at all.

clue.text: London Ranger is given advance short of one old penny

indicators.note: short of means without, so the pieces for one and old penny are removed

parts.note: to be loaned is to be given an advance of money
I is the Roman numeral for one
d is the abbreviation for a penny in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: A London park ranger gets a cash advance a penny short.
explanation.walkthrough: A Sloane Ranger is a stereotypical posh young Londoner from around Sloane Square in Chelsea; ISLOANED loses I and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloane Ranger was the 1980s nickname for upper-class young people living in Chelsea.

clue.text: As veteran cast of Mousetrap finally revealed?

definitions.text: As veteran cast of Mousetrap finally revealed?

parts.words: As veteran cast of Mousetrap finally revealed?
parts.note: The Mousetrap is Agatha Christie's play running in London since 1952, so its veteran cast are in a lengthy run; the phrase also means eventually

explanation.walkthrough: The Mousetrap is the world's longest-running play, a whodunit whose killer is unmasked at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means eventually, over a long period, the way a mystery is solved at the end.

clue.text: Departure, say, top papers ignored

parts.note: e.g. means for example, which say also means

indicators.note: top means the first letter, the top of a down entry
ignored means that first letter is left out

parts.note: the press means the newspapers

explanation.surface: A departure, for example, ignored by the leading newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: An egress is an exit or way out, the act of going out.

clue.text: Ace character initiated by Connery licensed to kill Blofeld's Number Two

indicators.note: the character that begins the word Connery is its first letter

parts.note: a 00 number marks a British agent licensed to kill, like James Bond, 007

indicators.note: Number Two points to the second letter of Blofeld's

explanation.surface: A Bond film pitch: Sean Connery's agent kills Blofeld's henchman.
explanation.walkthrough: Sean Connery played James Bond, whose 00 code means licensed to kill; Blofeld is Bond's arch-villain.
explanation.definitionFit: Ace and cool are both slang for excellent or great.

clue.text: Little brother has to have toast

parts.note: Br is the short form, a little version, of brother
to own is to have or possess

explanation.surface: A little brother must have some toast.
explanation.definitionFit: To toast is to brown bread under heat, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Trainspotter's not heading for a road

indicators.note: not heading means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: ane is the Scots word for one or a

explanation.surface: A trainspotter is heading somewhere other than a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not heading' drops A from ANE, the Scots form of 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainspotter is the stock image of an obsessive geek with a niche hobby.

clue.text: Rocker seized by one looking to influence opinions?

indicators.note: seized by means the rocker is held inside the word for one looking

parts.note: a seer is one who sees or looks
a logan, or logan stone, is a balanced boulder that rocks

explanation.surface: A rock musician is grabbed by someone trying to sway public views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocker' wants a musician, but it is a logan stone, a balanced boulder found in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloganeer coins catchy phrases for campaigns, trying to sway public views.

clue.text: See 21
It normally shows you've more than one mail

definitions.text: It normally shows you've more than one
definitions.meaning: split 6,1 this is the ..., which usually marks a plural
post, the things the postman delivers

explanation.walkthrough: Split as LETTER S, the first part is the letter that normally makes a word plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Post delivered through the door consists mostly of envelopes with correspondence inside.
